# kanok-ui (@purpurabog/ui 2.3.0)

> Carbon Design System components for any web app: Lit web components (`<ui-button>`, any framework), React wrappers, unstyled React parts (headless) and React + Tailwind components you copy in with shadcn. Themes white / g10 / g90 / g100, layers, Thai and English. npm package `@purpurabog/ui`; shadcn registry namespace `@kanok-ui`.

Rules for writing code with it: use these components instead of raw HTML controls; colour and space with the `--ui-*` tokens (never hard-coded colours); restyle with `::part()` and tokens, not the shadow DOM; nest `<ui-layer>` (or React `Layer`) for surfaces on surfaces. Each page below has an Installation section (npm and shadcn commands) and an API section (attributes, properties, events, slots, parts). The design tokens and rules are in [DESIGN.md](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/DESIGN.md) (also in the package: `node_modules/@purpurabog/ui/DESIGN.md`). Thai versions of every page are under `th/`.

## Get started

- [@purpurabog/ui](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/index.md): Components that follow IBM's Carbon Design System, made for forms in Thai and English: fields, lists, dates (Buddhist era), overlays, data tables and the UI shell. This site is built with them.
- [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation.md): The package is public on npm. Pick the way that fits your app; you can mix them.
- [Migrating to 1.0](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/migration-1-0.md): 1.0 replaces the data-driven web component `<ui-data-table>` with a family of elements that follow Carbon web components (`cds-table`): `<ui-table>`, `<ui-table-head>`, `<ui-table-header-row>`, `<ui-table-header-cell>`,…

## Guides

- [Themes and layers](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/themes.md): Every color comes from Carbon's four themes, generated from `@carbon/themes` into `tokens.css`. You pick a theme with one attribute, `data-theme`, on the whole page or on any part of it. Inside a theme, `<ui-layer>` moves fields and…
- [Kanok design](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/kanok.md): Kanok (กนก, after the flame-like Thai motif *lai kanok*) is the library's own style, next to Carbon. It is meant for internal business tools: clean and calm, surfaces set apart by their fill rather than lines, with a Thai-craft identity…
- [Customize the look](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/customizing.md): Start from the shallowest layer and go deeper only when it isn't enough:
- [Icons](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/icons.md): The components don't ship icons; they take yours in a slot or an `icon` prop and size and color them. Use Carbon's icons, the set this design system is drawn with: browse them in the IBM UI icon library and install the package for your…
- [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms.md): Every field is a form-associated custom element: it takes part in a plain `<form>` the way `<input>` does. You get submit, `FormData`, reset and the browser's constraint validation without any glue code.
- [Using it with frameworks](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/frameworks.md): The components are standard custom elements (`<ui-date-picker>`, `<ui-table>` …), so any framework that renders HTML can use them. React gets typed wrappers on top. This page covers what changes from one framework to the next: passing…
- [Use it with AI coding tools](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/ai.md): Claude, Cursor, Copilot and other AI tools write better code with these components when they can read the docs and the design rules. Give them three things: the docs index, the design file, and a short set of rules in your project.

## Forms and actions

- [Button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/button.md): A button starts an action: save, submit, open a dialog. For going to another page, give it an `href` and it becomes a real link.
- [Text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-input.md): A text input takes one line of text: a name, an email, a password, an ID number. For several lines, use a text area; for amounts, a number input.
- [Text area](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-area.md): A text area takes text that runs over several lines: notes, a description, a reason. It has the same label, helper text and error line as the text input, plus a character or word counter and a field that can grow with its text.
- [Number input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/number-input.md): A number input takes a number: a quantity, an amount, a percentage. Carbon's − and + buttons sit at the end of the field, and ↑ / ↓ step from the keyboard.
- [Search](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/search.md): A search field lets people find or filter content by typing. Carbon hides its label and shows a magnifier instead; a clear button appears once there is text.
- [Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/select.md): A select picks one option from a list. It wraps the browser's own `<select>`, so phones open their native picker and screen readers know it well.
- [Dropdown](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/dropdown.md): A dropdown picks one option from a list that looks the same in every browser. Options can have a second line and sit in labelled groups.
- [Combobox](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/combobox.md): A combobox is a text box with a list: people type to find an option instead of scrolling. Use it for long lists, server lookups, and fields that also take free text.
- [Multi-select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/multi-select.md): A multi-select picks several options from a list of checkbox rows. The list stays open while people choose, and a tag in the field shows how many are chosen.
- [Checkbox](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/checkbox.md): A checkbox turns one option on or off. In a group, people can pick any number of options, including none.
- [Radio button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/radio.md): Radio buttons pick exactly one option from a small set, with every option in view. Once one is picked, the user can change it but not clear it.
- [Toggle](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toggle.md): A toggle switches a setting on or off, and the change takes effect right away. The label sits above the switch and the state text beside it.
- [Date picker](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/date-picker.md): A date picker takes a date that users type or pick from a calendar. On a Thai page it shows the Buddhist era (พ.ศ.); your code always gets an ISO date in the Gregorian year.
- [Time picker](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/time-picker.md): A time picker takes a time as short `hh:mm` text, with optional selects beside it for AM / PM and the time zone.
- [Slider](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/slider.md): A slider picks a number, or a range between two numbers, from a scale. A number box beside the track lets users type the exact value.
- [File uploader](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/file-uploader.md): A file uploader lets people pick files from their device, with a button or by dropping them on a drop zone. The chosen files are listed under it, each with its state: ready, uploading, uploaded, or an error.

## Overlays

- [Modal](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/modal.md): A modal asks for the user's full attention: it opens over the page, the page behind it can't be used, and focus stays inside until it closes. Use it for a short task or a decision. For a long form or a flow with steps, use a Tearsheet;…
- [Side panel](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/side-panel.md): A side panel slides in from the edge of the screen, under the 48px UI shell header, to show details or a short form while the page stays in view. It is Carbon for IBM Products' `SidePanel`. For a task that needs the whole screen, use a…
- [Tearsheet](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tearsheet.md): A tearsheet is a large modal that rises from the bottom of the screen over the dimmed page. Use it for a task that needs room but keeps the user in the same place: creating a record, a form in several sections, a review with a side pane.…
- [Notification](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/notification.md): A notification tells the user about a change or a problem: a file that failed to upload, a draft that was restored, a policy that applies to the page. One element covers Carbon's inline, actionable, toast and callout notifications. For…
- [Toast](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toast.md): A toast is a short message that appears in the corner of the screen after something happened elsewhere on the page: a contract saved, an upload that failed in the background. Toasts stack, the newest nearest the corner, and the quiet…
- [Tooltip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tooltip.md): A tooltip is a short line of plain text about the control it wraps. It opens when the pointer rests on the control or keyboard focus reaches it, and closes when they leave. Use it to name an icon or add a hint, never for content people…
- [Definition tooltip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/definition-tooltip.md): A definition tooltip explains a word in running text. The word gets a dotted underline; a click, Enter or Space shows its definition in a dark bubble below it. Use it for terms readers may not know, such as legal or internal words.
- [Popover](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/popover.md): A popover is a floating box with your own content beside a trigger: a few filters, a short form, settings for a table. It is Carbon's `Popover`, the box behind tooltips, toggletips and menus. You decide when it opens; `auto-close` lets…
- [Toggletip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toggletip.md): A toggletip is a small "i" button that opens an explanation when clicked. Unlike a tooltip, it stays open until the user closes it, and it may hold links and buttons. Put it next to a label or a heading that needs more context.
- [Menu](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/menu.md): A menu is a short list of actions that opens from a button. This page covers the three triggers Carbon ships (the menu button, the overflow menu "⋮" and the combo button), the items that go inside them, and the menu on its own.

## Data

- [Data table](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/data-table.md): A data table shows rows of records in columns (Carbon `DataTable`). The web component follows Carbon web components (`cds-table`): you write the table as elements — `<ui-table-head>` with the header cells, `<ui-table-body>` with rows of…
- [Structured list](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/structured-list.md): A structured list shows a few rows of text in columns, for example to compare plans or to show the terms of a contract. It is lighter than a data table: no sorting, no toolbar. With `selection`, the user picks one row.
- [Pagination](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/pagination.md): Pagination splits a long list into pages: "Items per page", the range shown, a page select and previous / next buttons (Carbon `Pagination`). Put it under a table or a list. It only holds the page and the page size; showing the right…
- [Contained list](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/contained-list.md): A contained list is a titled list of rows separated by thin rules, for settings panels, side panels and tiles (Carbon `ContainedList`). A row can carry an icon and an action, or be a button itself.
- [Tree view](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tree-view.md): A tree view shows nested items, such as folders, a chart of accounts or an organisation's departments (Carbon `TreeView`). Branches open and close; the user selects a node with a click or the keyboard.

## Navigation

- [Tabs](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tabs.md): Tabs split related content into views on one page. One tab is selected at a time, and only its panel shows. A `disabled` tab stays in the strip but can't be chosen.
- [Breadcrumb](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/breadcrumb.md): A breadcrumb shows where the current page sits in the site's hierarchy, and links back up to each level above it. Put it at the top of the page, above the title.
- [Link](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/link.md): A link takes the user to another page, another place on this page, or a file. It is blue, underlines on hover and focus, and has Carbon's focus ring.
- [Pagination nav](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/pagination-nav.md): Pagination nav moves between numbered pages: Previous, the page numbers, and Next. The pages that don't fit fold into "…" menus at either end. `page` is 0-based, as in Carbon.
- [Content switcher](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/content-switcher.md): A content switcher shows the same content in another way: a filter (all requests or only mine) or a view (table or grid). Exactly one item is selected, and the switch happens at once.
- [Accordion](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/accordion.md): An accordion is a vertical list of headings. Each heading shows or hides the content under it, so a long page shows only the parts the reader asks for. Several items can be open at once.
- [Progress indicator](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/progress-indicator.md): A progress indicator shows where the user is in a task of several steps: which steps are done, which one is current and what comes next. Use it above a multi-step form or a wizard.
- [UI shell](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/ui-shell.md): The UI shell is the frame of an application: a 48px header fixed at the top, a side navigation on the left and the content area beside them. The header holds the product name, the main menu bar and icon buttons for global actions; the…

## Content

- [Tag](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tag.md): A tag labels and sorts things: a contract's status, the departments it belongs to, the filters on a list. It is read-only by default. It can also close (dismissible), turn on and off (selectable) or open something (operational).
- [Tile](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tile.md): A tile is a plain box on the next layer colour: 16px padding, no border, no shadow. It groups content on a dashboard or a summary page. With `href` the whole tile becomes one link. Carbon has four more kinds; here they are…
- [Card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/card.md): A card is a box built from parts: media, a header with a title and its actions, a body and a footer. Use it for a set of things the user browses or picks from: projects, reports, documents. It is Carbon's `Card` (a preview in Carbon):…
- [Product card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/product-card.md): `ui-productive-card` and `ui-expressive-card` are Carbon for IBM Products' `ProductiveCard` and `ExpressiveCard`: cards you configure with attributes, not with parts. They are IBM Products' legacy cards, kept for screens that must match…
- [Code snippet](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/code-snippet.md): A code snippet shows code or a command that people copy: an install line, a config file, an ID inside a sentence. It has three types: `single` (one line), `multi` (a block that folds after 15 rows) and `inline` (a chip in running text).…
- [Copy button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/copy-button.md): A copy button puts a value on the clipboard: a request number, a link, an API key. It is Carbon's 40px icon button: its tooltip names it ("Copy to clipboard"), and after a copy the tooltip says "Copied!" for two seconds.
- [User avatar](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/user-avatar.md): A user avatar is a round picture of a person: their photo, their initials, or a user icon. It comes from Carbon for IBM Products. Use it next to a name in approval chains, comments, owners of a record, and the header's account button.
- [Truncated text](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/truncated-text.md): Truncated text cuts a long text to a few lines with an ellipsis, and only when it doesn't fit, lets the user read the rest: in a tooltip, or with a "View more" toggle. It comes from Carbon for IBM Products. Use it for descriptions and…
- [List](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/list.md): Carbon's lists show related items in running content: steps to follow, conditions, documents to attach. `ui-unordered-list` marks each item with an en dash, `ui-ordered-list` numbers them, and `ui-list-item` is one item. A list inside an…

## Status and loading

- [Loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/loading.md): A loading spinner says that a view or an area is waiting for data. Carbon's spinner is 88px; `small` is 16px with a grey track. It can cover the whole page (`overlay`) or one area (`contained`), and it can wait before it shows, so quick…
- [Inline loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/inline-loading.md): Inline loading shows the progress of one action in place, such as saving or sending: a 16px spinner with a short text beside it. It moves from `active` to `finished` (a check mark) or `error`, and screen readers hear each change.
- [Progress bar](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/progress-bar.md): A progress bar shows how far a task has come, such as an upload or an import. The track fills to `value / max`; with no `value` a stripe sweeps across it while the length is unknown. A label names it, and helper text below says the details.
- [Skeleton](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/skeleton.md): A skeleton is a grey placeholder in the shape of the content to come, shown while a page loads its data for the first time. `<ui-skeleton>` draws text lines, a heading, a field, a button or a block. Most components also have their own…
- [Badge indicator](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/badge-indicator.md): A badge indicator is the small red mark in the corner of a ghost icon button, for things that wait for the user, such as approvals or new messages. With a count it shows the number; without one it is a dot. It belongs on an icon button:…
- [Status indicator](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/status-indicator.md): A status indicator shows the state of something with a small coloured icon and a label, such as a job that succeeded or an incident's severity. `<ui-icon-indicator>` uses Carbon's status icons; `<ui-shape-indicator>` uses simple shapes…

## Layout

- [Grid](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/grid.md): The grid is Carbon's 2x Grid: 4 columns on small screens, 8 from 672px (`md`) and 16 from 1056px (`lg`), with 32px gutters. `<ui-grid>` holds `<ui-column>`s, and each column says how many columns it spans at each size. The tinted boxes…
- [Heading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/heading.md): `<ui-heading>` renders a heading at the right level without you counting: each `<ui-section>` around it goes one level deeper, so the same markup gives an `<h2>` on one page and an `<h4>` inside a nested panel. The type follows Carbon's…
- [Layer](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/layer.md): `<ui-layer>` is Carbon's Layer: everything inside it uses the theme's next layer set, so a field on a gray tile isn't the same gray as the tile. Fields, menus, borders, dividers and hover fills all follow it. The Themes and layers guide…
- [Action set](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/action-set.md): An action set is the row of large buttons at the foot of a side panel or a tearsheet (Carbon for IBM Products `ActionSet`). The buttons are 64px tall with their text at the top, split by thin lines, and they share the width by rules that…
- [Page header](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/page-header.md): The page header is the top of a page in a product (Carbon `PageHeader`, from Carbon for IBM Products): a breadcrumb bar, the page title with its actions and a short text, and a tab bar. It sticks as the page scrolls: the title and text…
- [Big number](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/big-number.md): A big number shows one key figure large, under a small label: active contracts, money spent, uptime (Carbon for IBM Products `BigNumber`). It shortens long numbers ("12.3K"), can show the value against a total ("12.3K/50.0K"), a…
- [Edit in place](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/edit-in-place.md): Edit in place shows a value as plain text that people can edit right where it is, without opening a form (Carbon for IBM Products `EditInPlace`). Hovered, it gets the field fill and an "Edit" button. Clicked or tabbed into, it becomes a…

## Headless

- [Headless](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless.md): `@purpurabog/ui/headless` is the behaviour of the components without their look: React parts that bring Carbon's keyboard, focus, ARIA, popup placement and form submit, and render no class at all. The markup, the labels, the messages and…
- [Headless Text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-text-input.md): `TextInput` is the behaviour of the styled Text input as unstyled React parts: an `<input>`, a button that shows or hides a password, and a mask that formats the value as the user types.
- [Headless Text area](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-text-area.md): `TextArea` is the behaviour of the styled Text area as unstyled React parts: a `<textarea>` that can grow with its text, and a soft character or word counter. An uncontrolled area, and its counter, go back to `defaultValue` when its form…
- [Headless Number input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-number-input.md): `NumberInput` is the behaviour of the styled Number input as unstyled React parts: an `<input>` with − and + buttons. ↑ / ↓ step from the field. A step stays within `min` and `max` and is rounded, and each button turns off at its end of…
- [Headless Search](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-search.md): `Search` is the behaviour of the styled Search as unstyled React parts: a `role="search"` landmark named by its label, an `<input type="search">`, a clear button, and the magnifier button of an expandable search. - [Headless Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-select.md): `Select` is the behaviour of the styled Select as one unstyled React part: a native `<select>` with your `<option>` and `<optgroup>` children, so the browser gives the list, the keyboard and the form. - [Headless Dropdown](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-dropdown.md): The `Dropdown` parts give you the behaviour of the styled Dropdown with no styles: a button with `role="combobox"` that opens a listbox in the top layer, the keyboard (arrows, Home / End, Page Up / Page Down, typing to jump), the…
- [Headless Combobox](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-combobox.md): The `Combobox` parts give you the behaviour of the styled Combobox with no styles: a text box with `role="combobox"`, a listbox in the top layer that typing narrows or only highlights, the keyboard, the rule for what leaving the field…

- [Headless Checkbox](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-checkbox.md): `Checkbox.Root` is the native `<input type="checkbox">` with no styles, so form submission, `required`, Space, labels and screen readers come from the browser. On top of that it adds `indeterminate` as a prop, a read-only state,…
- [Headless Radio button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-radio.md): `RadioGroup.Root` is a `role="radiogroup"` around native `<input type="radio">` items that share one `name`, so the browser gives the single Tab stop, the arrow keys and form submission. The parts add the group's value, a read-only…
- [Headless Toggle](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-toggle.md): The headless part is named `Switch`, as in Base UI, where "Toggle" means a pressed button. `Switch.Root` is a `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked`, so Space and Enter flip it.
